clue.text: Girl with nothing wherewith to secure her quarry

parts.note: a lass is a girl, a young woman
the figure zero, nothing, looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A cowgirl with no other tool sets out to catch her prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy's rope with a running noose is thrown to catch cattle or horses.

clue.text: Badge of rank for non-conformist priest

indicators.note: a nonconformist will not keep to the usual order, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dissenting clergyman is given some insignia of military rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-conformist' reads as a religious label for the priest, but it is the anagram signal for PRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeants and corporals show rank by chevrons sewn on the sleeve, each a band of braid.

clue.text: First-class student figuring as quarrelsome brawler

explanation.surface: A top-grade scholar is revealed as a pugnacious troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: At Cambridge a student gaining first-class honours in the mathematics Tripos is called a wrangler.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge's title for a first in mathematics; also simply one who wrangles, that is, argues noisily.

clue.text: Dressing musicians on maturity

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians
age can mean the state of being old or mature, as in 'come of age'

explanation.surface: Musicians getting dressed as they grow older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressing' looks like putting on clothes, but it is the medical sense: a covering for a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound dressing is a strip of gauze or cloth wrapped round an injury.

clue.text: Recline restfully and get a cut of bacon

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes in a chair and buys some rashers.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit back at ease; and back bacon from the loin, trimmed of fat, sold as a lean cut.

clue.text: Andrew involved with Ida in Teddy boy style

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so the two names are jumbled into one another

explanation.surface: A man and a woman are caught up together in a 1950s youth fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles the letters of ANDREW and IDA together. Teddy boys were 1950s British youths who wore revived early-1900s fashions; 'Teddy' is a pet form of Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy boy clothing imitated the fashion of King Edward VII's reign, the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Principal male person prepared by one who booked Peter Simple

definitions.text: by one who booked Peter Simple

parts.note: a master is a head or principal, as of a school or college
a man is a male person

explanation.surface: A leading man is made ready by someone who reserved a seat for a person called Peter Simple.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Frederick Marryat wrote the novel Peter Simple, and also Masterman Ready, so the definition is 'a book by the author of Peter Simple'; 'booked' means wrote a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Marryat's 1841 children's novel of a shipwrecked family, from the author of Peter Simple.

clue.text: See 7
Short hair contents one-time Siamese native

indicators.note: contents are what is held inside, so the answer is found inside these two words

explanation.surface: A cat breed with short fur, contented, once from Siam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short hair' sounds like a cat breed next to 'Siamese', but the letters run across 'shorT HAIr'.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam was renamed Thailand in 1939, so a former Siamese is now a person from Thailand.

clue.text: Appointed formally as name is written

parts.note: when a name is written on a document it has been signed

explanation.surface: Someone is officially given a post when the document bears their signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Allotted or designated to a role or task by official decision.

clue.text: She has aspirations about oriental money

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two letters go round the coin

parts.note: an aspirate is the breathed sound of the letter H, so two aspirations give two Hs
an anna was a coin of India, a sixteenth of a rupee

explanation.surface: A woman with ambitions concerning Eastern finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspirations' looks like hopes, but it means the sound H, given twice; 'about' puts them round ANNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so a female person, 'she'.

clue.text: Healthy source of drink?

explanation.surface: A question whether a fit person is where refreshment comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: In good health; and a shaft sunk to reach underground water for drinking.

clue.text: The reigning house of Monaco as seen on 19th century stage

explanation.surface: Monaco's ruling family seen performing in Victorian theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Grimaldi was the famous English clown of the early 1800s pantomime stage, sharing a name with Monaco's ruling family.
explanation.definitionFit: The princely family ruling Monaco since the 1290s; and the name of the great Regency-era pantomime clown.

clue.text: Impudent epithet for one whose cheek lacks whiskers

definitions.text: epithet for one whose cheek lacks whiskers

explanation.surface: A cheeky person described by their clean-shaven face.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameless, bold without disguise; and literally of a face without a beard.

clue.text: Portable power pack enclosing many layers

explanation.surface: A pack of cells, wrapped in many coatings, supplies power on the go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' looks like strata, but here they are hens that lay eggs, kept in battery cages.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack of electric cells; and a row of small cages housing egg-laying hens.

clue.text: Forbidden formerly to set in consecutive order

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden
late means former, as in 'the late president'

explanation.surface: Something once banned is now allowed to be put in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange data in rows and columns, an ordered table.

clue.text: He goes ahead with light service and holds the programme together

definitions.text: He goes ahead with light service

explanation.surface: A man walks ahead with a lamp and also keeps a show running.
explanation.walkthrough: A link was a torch, and a link-boy or link-man was paid to light people's way through dark streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The old torch-bearer hired to light the way; and a broadcast presenter who connects the parts of a show.

clue.text: Commonly known as grass in earlier description

parts.note: former describes something from an earlier time

explanation.surface: A police informant described in slang from a past era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' is British slang for someone who tells the police about criminals; 'Commonly known as' marks the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tells the police about criminals, called a grass in British slang.

clue.text: He attends the match while another wins the girl

definitions.text: He attends the match while another wins the girl

parts.words: He attends the match while another wins the girl
parts.note: the match is a wedding, and he is called the best yet the bride goes to his friend

explanation.surface: A man at a sports fixture watches a rival win his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a game, but it is a marriage; the joke is that he is called best while the groom gets the bride.
explanation.definitionFit: The groom's chief attendant at a wedding, who supports him through the ceremony.

clue.text: Drop-leaf table from Dyfed

explanation.surface: A folding table comes from west Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Dyfed was a Welsh county (1974-96) that included the town of Pembroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A small table with hinged flaps on each side; and the Welsh town or old county, in Dyfed.

clue.text: Not even the balance of advantage

explanation.surface: The advantage is not evenly balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers not divisible by two; and the margin by which one side is favoured, as in betting.

clue.text: The office scraper

explanation.surface: A tool for scraping in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: A folder or record kept in an office; and a toothed steel tool for smoothing.

clue.text: Ale not otherwise adapted to penthouse living

indicators.note: otherwise and adapted both say these letters are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drinker adapts to luxury rooftop living without beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penthouse' looks like a luxury top flat, but its old sense is a shed with a sloping roof built against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Penthouse originally meant a sloping-roofed annexe resting against a larger building.

clue.text: Ecclesiastically, Salisbury written up as peculiar

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the word is set upward, read in reverse

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: The church's records show Salisbury as an odd place.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarum is the old Latin name for Salisbury, used by bishops who sign 'Sarum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bishops of Salisbury sign with the Latin name, and the medieval church rite is the Use of Sarum.

clue.text: Sentimental song as publicity for the dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A soppy song used as an advert for the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow romantic popular song, or a narrative poem set to music.

clue.text: The French in plaid muslin

indicators.note: in places the French article inside the cloth pattern

parts.note: tartan is plaid, Scottish checked cloth

explanation.surface: French people dressed in checked cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, stiffened open-weave cotton fabric used for ball gowns.

clue.text: Poetically lower than a Welsh town

explanation.surface: A Welsh town lies below, in poetic phrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic short form of beneath; and a town in South Wales near Swansea.

clue.text: How to settle a dispute: get rid of that aching tooth

definitions.text: get rid of that aching tooth

explanation.surface: Advice for ending a row: have that painful tooth pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue a matter through openly; and literally to have the tooth extracted.
